Model-Assisted Stratified Estimator

Source: R/est_functions.R
est_ma_strat.Rd

Computes the model-assisted treatment effect estimator that combines surrogate predictions for the full population with a bias correction from a human-coded stratified subsample. Within each treatment arm and stratum, the estimator adjusts the population mean of surrogate scores by the average residual (human score minus surrogate) in the coded units, weighted by stratum sizes.

est_ma_strat(
  data = NULL,
  Yhat = "Yhat",
  Yobs = "Yobs",
  S = "S",
  Z = "Z",
  strata = "strata",
  return_pieces = FALSE,
  finite_pop = FALSE
)

Arguments

data

Data frame containing outcome, surrogate, sampling indicator, treatment, and stratification columns.

Yhat

Name of the surrogate score column. Default is "Yhat".

Yobs

Name of the human-coded outcome column. Default is "Yobs".

S

Name of the sampling indicator column (1 = coded, 0 = not coded). Default is "S".

Z

Name of the treatment indicator column, or NULL for a population mean. Default is "Z".

strata

Name of the stratification column, or NULL for unstratified (SRS) estimation. Default is "strata".

return_pieces

Logical. If TRUE, returns a list with intermediate quantities useful for diagnostics. Default is FALSE.

finite_pop

Logical. If TRUE, applies finite population corrections and returns only the sampling variance component. Default is FALSE.

Value

A data frame with columns:

est

Point estimate of the treatment effect (or mean).

SE

Oracle SE computed using true residual variances for all units.

SEhat

Estimated SE from the coded subsample, combining both the full-coding and sampling variance components.

SEhat.full

Estimated SE component attributable to treatment effect variability (i.e., variance even if all units were coded).

SEhat.samp

Estimated SE component attributable to subsampling (i.e., additional variance from coding only a subset).

S2.0, S2.1

Estimated population variance of outcomes in control and treatment groups.

Details

If strata is set to NULL, this reduces to the SRS model-assisted estimator (equivalent to calling est_ma_srs()).

See also

est_ma_srs() for the unstratified version, est_subset() for the baseline estimator, and generate_sample_index() for drawing stratified samples.
